dedupe_keys.name: radio kpi throughput and latency of 5g and satellite links for livestock transport monitoring in rural denmark commect aalborg university

description: Two measurement datasets from a campaign in northern Denmark that tested a multi-connectivity solution, combining two 5G non-standalone cellular operators and a satellite link, for monitoring livestock transport in rural areas. The Zenodo records say each row is a timestamped data point with RSRP, RSRQ and signal-to-noise ratio, plus throughput in Mbps in one dataset and two-way latency in milliseconds in the other. They were produced by the Denmark Living Lab of the Horizon Europe COMMECT project and published by Aalborg University on 9 January 2025 as post-processed data, each a downloadable ZIP (5.1 MB and 2.4 MB) that also contains the related research papers, under CC BY-SA 4.0. Coverage is a rural area of northern Denmark during one campaign. Caveats: operators and routes are not named, the campaign dates are not stated on the records read, and the share-alike licence applies. For simulation it gives measured link quality and latency for terrestrial and low Earth orbit satellite backup in rural farm logistics, to model connectivity failover and the resilience of livestock and food transport monitoring. A related catalogue record is the GRDC Grain Automate farm connectivity metrics.
